builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier
summary: The method replaces proxy-based explanation scoring and frontier-model distillation with exact algorithmic verification of minimal sufficient reasons for policy decisions. It requires an enumerable context space and executable policy to compute ground truth, plus 2000 verified traces for fine-tuning a 4B model, fitting within a 24GB GPU budget. Learned schedules overfit to the training policy and fail to transfer: answers remain sufficient but stop being minimal on unseen policies, and reinforcement learning from the exact reward inverts strategy without improving generalization.
rationale: While the exact verifier enables legible training signals, the learned behavior does not generalize across policies, making it unsuitable for production adoption without policy-specific retraining.

claims.statement: The method replaces proxy-based explanation scoring and frontier-model distillation with exact algorithmic verification of minimal sufficient reasons for policy decisions. It requires an enumerable context space and executable policy to compute ground truth, plus 2000 verified traces for fine-tuning a 4B model, fitting within a 24GB GPU budget. Learned schedules overfit to the training policy and fail to transfer: answers remain sufficient but stop being minimal on unseen policies, and reinforcement learning from the exact reward inverts strategy without improving generalization.

A 4B model fine-tuned on 2000 exact-verifier traces reaches 92% accuracy on the trained policy versus frontier models at roughly half, but drops to 48% minimality on unseen policies where Haiku 4.5 remains exact on all 47 episodes; RL from the exact reward does not improve held-out accuracy.
